title: Quantitative Immunoblotting Analysis of LRRK2 Signalling Pathway
author: Francesca Tonelli
materials: Immediately place the cell dishes On ice .
Scrape the cells on the dish using a cell lifter (Sigma-Aldrich CLS3008, or equivalent) to ensure all cells are detached from the dish.
ASAP Protocol Particulars: context and tips

steps.title: Pre-treat cells or tissues
steps.instruction: Treat samples to ensure specificity of phosphorylation signals before lysis.

substeps.instruction: For cultured cells: Treat for at least 30 min ± with a LRRK2 kinase inhibitor (e.g., MLi-2 at 100nM final concentration) or equivalent volume of DMSO vehicle.
For mouse tissues: Administer MLi-2 (30 mg/kg final dose) by subcutaneous injection 2 hours prior to tissue collection.

steps.title: Prepare cell lysates
steps.instruction: Extract proteins from cultured cells using ice-cold lysis buffer.

substeps.instruction: Quickly wash cells in the culture dish with room temperature, serum-free culture media (do not use PBS).

Aspirate all residual media and immediately add ice-cold lysis buffer to cover the entire surface. Guidelines: 0.1-0.2 ml per well of a 6-well plate, 0.5 ml for a 10 cm dish, and 1 ml for a 15 cm dish (aim for protein concentrations ≥ 0.75 µg/µl).

Transfer lysate to an Eppendorf tube on ice. For non-adherent cells: transfer to a Falcon tube, pellet by centrifugation at 180 x g for 3 minutes, wash once with room temperature serum-free media, pellet again, discard supernatant, and add ice-cold lysis buffer.
Incubate samples on ice for 20 minutes for efficient lysis.
Clarify lysates by centrifugation at 20,800 x g at 4 °C for 10 minutes.
Transfer supernatants to new Eppendorf tubes, discard the pellet, and keep on ice or snap freeze in liquid nitrogen and store at -80 °C.

steps.title: Prepare tissue lysates
steps.instruction: Extract proteins from mouse tissues using a pulverizer and lysis buffer.

substeps.instruction: Collect tissues from mice culled by cervical dislocation and snap freeze immediately in liquid nitrogen; store at -80 °C.
Grind frozen tissue to a fine powder using a pulverizer kit (maintain pulverizer units and spatula in liquid nitrogen).
Transfer tissue powder using a spatula to an Eppendorf tube on dry ice. Weigh the powder while keeping samples on dry ice.
Immediately add a 10-fold volume excess of ice-cold lysis buffer (e.g., 1000 μl buffer for 100 mg powder) and quickly vortex to mix.
Incubate samples on ice for 20 minutes for efficient lysis.
Clarify lysates by centrifugation at 20,800 x g at 4 °C for 30 minutes.
Transfer supernatants into new Eppendorf tubes and discard the pellet.

steps.title: Quantify protein concentration
steps.instruction: Determine protein concentration using a Bradford assay.

substeps.instruction: Perform Bradford assay in triplicate according to manufacturer's instructions.
Ensure samples are in the linear range; if not, dilute with water. Expected ranges: 0.5 to 5 µg/µl for near confluent cells and at least 2 µg/µl for tissues.

steps.title: Prepare samples for immunoblotting
steps.instruction: Normalize protein concentrations and denature samples.

substeps.instruction: Adjust all samples to the same protein concentration (ideally 0.5-2 µg/µl) by combining lysate with lysis buffer.
Add 4X SDS/LDS loading buffer freshly supplemented with beta-mercaptoethanol at a 1:4 ratio (e.g., 2.5 µl buffer for 7.5 µl lysate/buffer mix) and vortex.
Incubate samples for 5 minutes at 70 °C using a heating block.
Load samples onto a NuPAGE 4–12% Bis–Tris Midi Gel (ThermoFisherScientific, Cat#WG1402BOX or Cat#WG1403BOX) or a self-cast 10% Bis-Tris gel.
Include pre-stained molecular weight markers (10 kDa to 250 kDa).
Rinse wells with running buffer before loading.
Load 10-40 μg of protein per sample. For MEFs, A549, or human peripheral blood cells (monocytes, neutrophils), load 10-15 μg. For mouse brain, spleen, kidney, lung, and intestine, load 30-40 μg.
Include an internal loading control if using multiple gels.
Electrophorese at 130V with MOPS SDS running buffer for 2 hours or until the blue dye runs off the gel.

steps.title: Transfer proteins to membrane
steps.instruction: Perform wet electroblotting to transfer proteins to a nitrocellulose membrane.

substeps.instruction: Pre-soak the gel, one nitrocellulose membrane (GE Healthcare, Amersham Protran Supported 0.45 μm NC), and two pieces of filter paper (Whatman 3MM Chr Chromatography Paper) in transfer buffer.
Assemble the stack in a tray of transfer buffer: sponge pad (cathode side) → filter paper → gel → nitrocellulose membrane → filter paper → sponge pad. Use a roller to remove air bubbles.
Close the cassette, insert into the transfer tank, and fill with transfer buffer.
Transfer at 100 V (constant voltage) for 1 hour 40 minutes on ice.
Stain membranes with Ponceau solution to assess efficiency; scan if a record is required.

steps.title: Section membranes
steps.instruction: Divide the membrane into three sections for multiplexed antibody incubation.

substeps.instruction: Cut the membrane horizontally: one cut just above the 75 kDa marker and one just below the 37.5 kDa marker.
Top section: Top to 75 kDa (for LRRK2-total and LRRK2-pSer935).
Middle section: 75 kDa to 37.5 kDa (for alpha-tubulin or GAPDH).
Bottom section: 37.5 kDa to bottom (for Rab10-total/pThr73 or Rab12-total/pSer105). Note: Rab12 analysis requires duplicate gels.

steps.title: Block and incubate primary antibodies
steps.instruction: Block the membrane and incubate with specific primary antibodies.

substeps.instruction: Wash Ponceau-stained membranes with TBS-T and incubate in blocking solution for at least 15 minutes at room temperature on a see-saw rocker.

Rinse in TBS-T and incubate overnight at 4 °C with primary antibodies diluted in 5% (w/v) BSA in TBS-T. Use the following targets per section: Top (anti-total and phospho-LRRK2), Middle (anti-alpha tubulin or GAPDH), Bottom (anti-total and phospho-Rab).

Refer to Table 1 for dilutions: Rab10 pThr73 (Abcam ab230261, 1 µg/ml), Rab10 total (Nanotools 0680-100/Rab10-605B11 or Abcam ab237703, 1 µg/ml), Rab12 pSer105/106 (Abcam ab256487, 1 µg/ml), Rab12 total (MRC-PPU SA227 or Proteintech 18843-1-AP, 1 µg/ml), LRRK2 pSer935 (MRC-PPU UDD2, 1 µg/ml), LRRK2 total C-term (Antibodies Inc. 75-253, 1 µg/ml), LRRK2 total N-term (MRC-PPU UDD3, 0.1 µg/ml), GAPDH (Antibodies Inc. sc-32233, 1:5,000), alpha-tubulin (Cell Signaling 3873, 1:5,000).
Wash membranes in TBS-T three times for 5-10 minutes each on a see-saw rocker.

steps.title: Incubate secondary antibodies
steps.instruction: Apply fluorescent secondary antibodies for detection.

substeps.instruction: Incubate membranes with near-infrared fluorescent dye-labelled secondary antibodies (diluted 1:20,000) for 1 hour at room temperature on a see-saw rocker.
For multiplexing, use spectrally distinct dyes: IRDye 800CW (800 nm) for phospho-antibodies and IRDye 680LT (680 nm) for total antibodies.

Refer to Table 2 for secondary antibodies: goat anti-mouse IRDye 680LT (LI-COR 926-68020), goat anti-mouse IRDye 800CW (LI-COR 926-32210), goat anti-rabbit IRDye 800CW (LI-COR 926-32211), donkey anti-mouse IRDye 680LT (LI-COR 926-68022), donkey anti-mouse IRDye 800CW (LI-COR 926-32212), donkey anti-rabbit IRDye 800CW (LI-COR 926-32213), donkey anti-goat IRDye 800CW (LI-COR 926-32214 for Sheep primary Abs).
Wash membranes in TBS-T four times for 10-15 minutes each with agitation.

steps.title: Acquire and analyze images
steps.instruction: Detect protein bands and quantify signal intensity.

substeps.instruction: Acquire protein bands via near-infrared fluorescent detection using the Odyssey CLx Imaging System.
Quantify signal intensity using Image Studio Software, normalizing against the control sample to account for inter-gel variability.
Analyze data using statistical software such as Graphpad Prism.
